answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge whose seed is derived from its own past behavior; identical clones return identical answers, so the system flags any pair whose responses match across independent challenges. An attacker must make each clone diverge, which breaks the shared state that made cloning cheap—forcing a fresh juniper instance with unique history per identity. The zenith of clone count collapses to the number of genuinely distinct histories maintained. Hollow duplication becomes detectable at the first matched challenge,
